dimensional analysis of pendulum: T depends on L, m, g
  4 quantities, 3 independent dimensions (length, mass, time) → 4 − 3 = 1 dimensionless group
  (in SI dimensions: under units natural (ħ = c = 1) those constants are pure numbers, so length, mass and time would collapse into powers of energy and hide the groups)
  Π₁ = T √(g/L)
  so T ∝ √(L/g)   (T = C √(L/g), with C a pure number)
  m drops out: nothing else has mass
  defined pendulum(L, g) = √(L/g), so T = C pendulum(L, g)
0.319275 s
dimensional analysis of planck: l depends on G, ħ, c
  4 quantities, 3 independent dimensions (length, mass, time) → 4 − 3 = 1 dimensionless group
  (in SI dimensions: under units natural (ħ = c = 1) those constants are pure numbers, so length, mass and time would collapse into powers of energy and hide the groups)
  Π₁ = l √(c³/(G ħ))
  so l ∝ √(G ħ/c³)   (l = C √(G ħ/c³), with C a pure number)
  defined planck = √(G ħ/c³) = 8.19×10⁻²³ MeV⁻¹
1.616×10⁻³⁵ m
